# The Bukit Besi Tools

> 100 free online tools for code, SEO, writing, images and AI, plus Malaysian salary, zakat and BMI calculators. No signup needed.

This site hosts its own calculators and a directory of free tools, most of which run on https://www.thebukitbesi.com/. Tools on this site run in the browser and do not send inputs to this site. Last updated 2026-10-17.

## Tools and calculators on this site

- [Age Calculator Malaysia: Exact Age, Hijri Age and Next Birthday](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/age-calculator-malaysia/): Age calculator for Malaysia: exact age in years, months and days, total days, weeks and months, the next birthday and the weekday of birth, plus the age in Hijri years on Malaysia's official takwim (1979 to 2077) and the next Hijri birthday. Example: born 1 May 1990, on 15 October 2026 the age is 36 years 5 months 14 days (13,316 days), born on a Tuesday, next birthday 1 May 2027; Hijri date of birth 5 Syawal 1410H, Hijri age 37 years. Born on 29 February: the birthday falls on 1 March in common years. Official ages in Malaysia (verified 15 October 2026): first MyKad at 12 (MyKid before; free within 30 days of the 12th birthday); motorcycle learner licence B2 at 16 and car D at 17 (JPJ); 18 to vote with automatic registration (Undi18, in force 15 December 2021), stand for the Dewan Rakyat, the age of majority (Age of Majority Act 1971), replace the MyKad and buy tobacco and vape products (Act 852); 21 to buy alcohol (Food (Amendment) Regulations 2016); EPF: Akaun Sejahtera withdrawal once between 50 and 54, all accounts merge into Akaun 55 at 55; 60 is the minimum retirement age (Minimum Retirement Age Act 2012, also civil servants) and the senior citizen definition, with EPF Akaun Emas and the Rapid Emas 50% card.
- [Free AI Image Generator: Text to Image with FLUX, No Sign-Up](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/ai-image-generator/): Free AI image generator (text to image) using FLUX.1 [schnell] by Black Forest Labs on Cloudflare Workers AI. Type an idea in English or Bahasa Melayu; the optional 'Improve prompt' button uses a language model to translate and expand it into a detailed English prompt, which FLUX understands best. Ten one-tap styles add a tested style phrase: photo, cinematic, anime, 3D cartoon, watercolour, oil painting, Malaysian batik, pixel art, line art and flat poster. Quality: fast (4 steps) or detailed (8 steps, the model's maximum). Output is a square picture shown in the browser, with download and a strip of the last 6 pictures in the current tab; pictures and prompts are not stored by the site. Each connection may create up to 8 pictures a day (3 a minute) from a free daily allowance shared by all visitors that resets at 8am Malaysia time. Requests for sexual, nude or gory content are refused. FLUX.1 [schnell] is released under the Apache 2.0 licence.
- [AI Prompt Generator: Midjourney, Stable Diffusion, Veo, Sora](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/ai-prompt-generator/): Builds AI image and video prompts from a subject plus style, lighting, framing, lens, mood, colour, camera movement and speed choices, and writes them in each platform's own format with three variations (as chosen, cinematic, artistic): Midjourney with --ar, --no and --stylize parameters; Stable Diffusion as comma keywords with a separate negative prompt and a CLIP token count (it reads about 75 tokens); ChatGPT/DALL·E and Flux as plain sentences without negative prompts; Google Veo and Sora with camera, dialogue and audio lines; Runway with the camera move first and no negative wording; Kling with its own negative prompt box. Includes a seeded 'Surprise me', shareable links, saved prompts kept in the browser, and a hand-off from the Image to Prompt tool.
- [Free AI Summarizer: Summarize Articles, Essays and Notes Instantly](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/ai-summarizer/): Free AI text summarizer for English and Bahasa Melayu. Paste up to 12,000 characters (about 2,000 words) of an article, essay, report, meeting notes or chapter and choose a length (short: 2 to 3 sentences; medium: 5 to 7; detailed: 10 to 12) and a format (bullet points, one paragraph, or key points with a final takeaway line). The summary can be in the same language, in Malay or in English, so it also summarizes an English article in Malay. It shows the word count before and after, how much shorter the summary is and the reading time saved (at 230 words a minute). The model is told to use only information in the text and keep key names, numbers and dates. Runs on Cloudflare Workers AI (Mistral Small 3.1, Llama 3.3 70B fallback); the text is processed once and not stored. Free daily allowance shared by all visitors resets at 8am Malaysia time; each connection may make up to 40 AI requests a day.
- [Annual Leave Calculator Malaysia: Pro Rata Leave by the Employment Act](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/annual-leave-calculator-malaysia/): Calculates paid leave under Malaysia's Employment Act 1955 as amended from 1 January 2023 (it covers all employees): annual leave of 8 days a year with under 2 years' service, 12 days with 2 to under 5 years and 16 days with 5 years or more (s.60E); in a year of joining or leaving, leave is pro rata by completed months (entitlement × months ÷ 12), with a fraction of a day under one half disregarded and one half or more counted as a day; unused leave on leaving is paid at the ordinary rate of pay (monthly wages ÷ 26). Sick leave is 14, 18 or 22 days a year by the same service bands, plus 60 days of hospitalisation leave (s.60F); maternity leave is 98 days and paternity leave 7 days for married men with 12 months' service, for up to five confinements. Example: leaving on 30 June 2026 after 4 years 4 months gives 12 × 6 ÷ 12 = 6 days; with 3 taken, 3 days on RM3,900 a month are paid RM450 (RM150 a day). Joining on 1 April 2026 gives 8 × 9 ÷ 12 = 6 days for 2026.
- [Ar-Rahnu Calculator Malaysia 2026: Islamic Gold Pawn Charges](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/ar-rahnu-calculator-malaysia/): Ar-Rahnu (Islamic pawnbroking) calculator for Malaysia, verified 15 October 2026. Two charging models: banks using tawarruq (since Bank Negara Malaysia's Shariah Advisory Council ruling effective 1 February 2020) charge a yearly profit rate on the financing amount; non-bank operators charge a safekeeping fee (upah simpan) per RM100 of the gold's value (marhun) a month. Published rates: Bank Muamalat 11.25% a year, up to 80% of the gold's value, up to 18 months; Bank Islam up to 11.25% a year (ceiling), 80%; TEKUN RM0.50 per RM100 a month, 80%, 6 months extendable; YaPEIM Care RM0.75 and YaPEIM Bisnes RM1.00 per RM100 a month, 80%, 6 months. YaPEIM Didik RM0.85 (margin not confirmed). Bank Rakyat, Agrobank and MAIDAM do not publish a current rate. Example: RM6,000 of gold with 80% financing (RM4,800) for 6 months: Bank Muamalat RM45 a month (RM270), TEKUN RM30 (RM180), YaPEIM Care RM45 (RM270), YaPEIM Bisnes RM60 (RM360). A RM0.75 fee on the gold's value at 80% financing equals 11.25% a year on the financing. Conventional pawnshops may charge up to 2% a month on the loan under the Pawnbrokers Act 1972. If not redeemed, the gold is auctioned and any surplus is returned to the customer. The calculator values gold at the daily pure-gold price; each provider sets its own, usually lower, price per gram.
- [Arah Kiblat Malaysia: Cari Darjah Kiblat Lokasi Anda](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/arah-kiblat/): Mengira arah kiblat sebagai bearing awal bulatan besar dari utara benar ke Kaabah (21.4225° U, 39.8262° T), dengan jarak menggunakan formula haversine. Dari Kuala Lumpur, kiblat ialah 292° 32′ (292.54°, kira-kira 22.5° ke utara dari arah barat, barat barat laut), sejauh 6,974 km; Johor Bahru 292° 58′, George Town 291° 34′, Kota Bharu 291° 02′, Kuching 292° 07′ dan Kota Kinabalu 290° 37′. Di seluruh Malaysia, kiblat terletak antara kira-kira 290.5° dan 293° dari utara benar. Kompas telefon menunjuk utara magnet dan perlu ditentukur; bagi masjid atau surau, arah kiblat ditetapkan oleh jabatan mufti negeri. Dua kali setahun, semasa istiwa' a'zam (lewat petang waktu Malaysia sekitar 27–28 Mei dan 15–16 Julai), matahari tegak di atas Kaabah dan bayang objek tegak menghala bertentangan dengan kiblat.
- [ASB Dividend Calculator 2026: Yearly Payout, Projection & Loan](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/asb-dividend-calculator/): Calculates the Amanah Saham Bumiputera (ASB) income distribution (dividend plus bonus) from the average of each month's lowest balance, either from an opening balance and monthly saving or from twelve exact monthly lowest balances; projects the balance over up to 40 years with distributions reinvested and the RM200,000 input limit applied; and compares ASB financing instalments and interest with the distribution earned. Includes the ASB distribution history 2019–2025 (FY2025: 5.75 sen, 5.20 sen dividend + 0.55 sen bonus).
- [Assessment Tax Calculator Malaysia 2026: DBKL, MBPJ and MBPP Rates](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/assessment-tax-calculator-malaysia/): Malaysian assessment tax (cukai taksiran, cukai pintu) calculator, verified 15 October 2026. Under the Local Government Act 1976 (Act 171), yearly tax = annual value (the estimated gross rent a year, i.e. monthly rent × 12) × the council's rate (s.127, set by the council with state approval, at most 35% of annual value, s.130). Paid in two halves: by 28 February and 31 August; after that it becomes arrears (s.147) and each council sets its own late charges. Confirmed rates: DBKL 4% residential, 10% commercial; MBPJ (2025 valuation list) 4% landed, 3% apartment or condominium, 2% low-cost high-rise, 3.5% serviced apartment, with Selangor's 25% cap on increases from 1 January 2025; MBPP (from 1 January 2025) 5.6% landed, 5.0% low-cost and low-medium-cost landed, 5.0% low-cost and middle-class flats, 5.5% apartment or condominium, 9% commercial, 10.5% industrial. MBPJ example: annual value RM9,900 × 4% = RM396 a year (RM198 a half). Rent RM1,500 a month: DBKL RM720 a year, MBPP landed RM1,008. Councils in Johor and Melaka use improved value, not annual value; MBSA, MBSJ, MBKj and Putrajaya rates are entered by the user because sources are not yet sufficient.
- [BMI Calculator Malaysia: Asian Cut-offs, Healthy Weight, Waist](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/bmi-calculator-malaysia/): Calculates adult body mass index (BMI) in metric or imperial units and classifies it with the Malaysian Clinical Practice Guidelines on Management of Obesity (Asian cut-offs: underweight below 18.5, healthy 18.5–22.9, overweight 23.0–27.4, obese class I 27.5–34.9, class II 35.0–39.9, class III 40 and above) alongside the WHO international categories; gives the healthy weight range for the height and the kilograms to lose or gain, and checks waist circumference (risk from 90 cm in men and 80 cm in women) and waist-to-height ratio (NICE: keep the waist below half the height).
- [Bursa Share Fee Calculator: Brokerage, Stamp Duty and Profit](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/bursa-share-fee-calculator/): Calculates Bursa Malaysia share trading costs and profit. On each buy and each sell: brokerage (negotiable, set by each broker as a rate with a minimum per contract), a clearing fee of 0.03% of the contract value capped at RM1,000, and stamp duty on the contract note of 0.10% capped at RM1,000 for listed shares (remission order P.U.(A) 208/2023, 13 July 2023 to 12 July 2028; the statutory rate is RM1.50 per RM1,000). 8% service tax applies to brokerage and clearing on ETFs, REITs, warrants and similar securities; brokers do not charge it on ordinary shares. Example: 1,000 shares bought at RM2.00 and sold at RM2.30 with 0.08% brokerage and an RM8 minimum: buy charges RM10.60, sell charges RM10.99, net profit RM278.41 (13.85%), break-even selling price RM2.022. Single-tier dividends are tax-free for individuals up to RM100,000 a year, with 2% on the excess from YA2025; gains on listed shares are not subject to capital gains tax.
- [Calorie Calculator Malaysia: BMR, Daily Calories and Weight Loss](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/calorie-calculator-malaysia/): Calorie calculator for Malaysians, verified 15 October 2026. Basal metabolic rate (BMR) by the Mifflin-St Jeor equation (1990): men 10 × weight (kg) + 6.25 × height (cm) − 5 × age + 5; women the same but −161. Daily need = BMR × activity factor: 1.2 sedentary, 1.375 lightly active (exercise 1 to 3 days a week), 1.55 moderately active (3 to 5 days), 1.725 very active (6 to 7 days), 1.9 extra active. Losing 0.5 kg a week needs about 550 kcal a day less (about 7,700 kcal per kg). Example: a man aged 30, 70 kg, 170 cm, moderately active: BMR 1,618 kcal, daily need 2,508 kcal, 1,958 kcal to lose 0.5 kg a week. A woman aged 30, 60 kg, 158 cm, sedentary: BMR 1,277 kcal, daily need 1,532 kcal. Macronutrient split by the Recommended Nutrient Intakes for Malaysia (RNI 2017): carbohydrate 50 to 65%, protein 10 to 20%, fat no more than 30% of energy. RNI 2017 for ages 19 to 29 at physical activity levels 1.4/1.6/1.8/2.0: men 1,960/2,240/2,520/2,800 kcal, women 1,610/1,840/2,080/2,310 kcal. BMI by the Malaysian CPG Asian cut-offs: below 18.5 underweight, 18.5 to 22.9 normal, 23 to 27.4 overweight, 27.5 and above obese. Malaysian Healthy Plate: a quarter rice or grains, a quarter protein, half vegetables and fruit.
- [AI Caption Generator for Instagram and TikTok, with Hashtags](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/caption-generator/): Free AI caption and hashtag generator for Malaysians. Describe the post in a few words and choose the platform (Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, X, LinkedIn, Threads), tone (casual, funny, inspiring, selling, grateful, romantic, professional), language (English, Bahasa Melayu, Manglish or rojak), occasion (Hari Raya Aidilfitri, Aidiladha, Ramadan, Merdeka, Chinese New Year, Deepavali, New Year, birthday, wedding, graduation, travel, food) and emoji on or off. It writes 5 different captions, each with its own copy button and a character count against the platform limit, plus hashtags capped at the platform maximum. Limits used (verified 16 October 2026): Instagram captions 2,200 characters and at most 5 hashtags per post (Instagram's change from 30, announced 18 December 2025), about 125 characters shown before 'more'; TikTok video captions 2,200 characters (official API limit; many accounts get 4,000 in the app) and at most 5 hashtags (from July 2025); X 280 characters (25,000 for Premium); LinkedIn 3,000; Threads 500; Facebook 63,206. Runs on Cloudflare Workers AI; nothing is stored.
- [Car Loan Calculator Malaysia 2026: Instalment, Interest, Insurance](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/car-loan-calculator-malaysia/): Calculates Malaysian car loan (hire purchase) instalments by the reducing-balance method with an effective interest rate (EIR), required by the Hire-Purchase (Amendment) Act from 1 June 2026 with a transition to 31 March 2027, or by the older flat-rate method; converts flat rate to EIR and back; shows total interest, a yearly schedule and the early settlement amount, including the Rule of 78 rebate for older flat-rate agreements; also estimates JPJ road tax by engine cc (Peninsular saloon or non-saloon, Sabah and Sarawak saloon) or by motor power for electric cars up to 310 kW and comprehensive insurance with NCD, 8% SST and stamp duty, and the total monthly cost of owning the car.
- [Case Converter: Title Case, Sentence Case, camelCase and More](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/case-converter/): Free online case converter that runs in the browser. Text cases: Sentence case (capitalises after full stops, question marks and line breaks, and the pronoun I), Title Case following AP style (articles a, an, the and conjunctions and prepositions of three letters or fewer such as and, but, for, in, of, on, to stay lowercase unless first or last, or after a colon), UPPERCASE, lowercase, Capitalize Each Word, alternating and inverse case. Acronyms such as SEO, EPF or KWSP are kept in capitals unless the whole text is in capitals. Developer cases: camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, CONSTANT_CASE, kebab-case, Train-Case, dot.case, path/case and URL slugs (accents removed, & becomes and); words are split at spaces, punctuation and camelCase humps, and each line converts separately. Also cleans extra spaces and has undo.
- [CGPA Calculator: SGPA to CGPA and GPA from Grades](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/cgpa-calculator/): Calculates CGPA from semester SGPAs (credit-weighted, or a simple average without credits) and GPA/CGPA from course letter grades on the UGC 10-point scale (O, A+, A … P, F) or the Malaysian 4.00 scale (A 4.00, A− 3.67, B+ 3.33 …), including continuing from a previous CGPA.
- [CGPA to Percentage Calculator: VTU, AKTU, SPPU, CBSE & More](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/cgpa-to-percentage/): Converts CGPA to percentage (and percentage back to CGPA) with the formula each university commonly publishes: CBSE CGPA × 9.5, VTU/AKTU/MAKAUT/SPPU (CGPA − 0.75) × 10, GTU (CGPA − 0.5) × 10, University of Mumbai CGPA × 7.1 + 11, Anna University CGPA × 10, any-scale proportional and custom formulas, with a full CGPA 5.0–10.0 conversion table.
- [City-Link Tracking: Track Your City-Link Express Parcel](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/citylink-tracking/): City-Link Express tracking: opens City-Link's official tracking page for a consignment number, explains the number format, common statuses, what to do when a delivery fails, and background on City-Link Express, founded in 1979 as Malaysia's first locally owned courier.
- [Color Contrast Checker: WCAG AA and AAA Contrast Ratio](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/color-contrast-checker/): Free color contrast checker using the WCAG 2.2 formula: contrast ratio (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05) from relative luminance. Pass or fail for AA normal text (4.5:1), AA large text (3:1; large is at least 24px, or 18.66px bold), AAA normal text (7:1), AAA large text (4.5:1) and non-text UI components and graphics (3:1, SC 1.4.11). Ratios are truncated, not rounded up, so 4.499 fails. Accepts hex, rgb(), hsl() and CSS color names; transparent colors are blended over the background. Suggests the nearest passing text or background color keeping the same hue. Simulates protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia (Machado et al. 2009). Checks every pair in a palette of up to 8 colors. Reference values: #767676 on white is 4.54:1, the lightest grey that passes AA for normal text; #595959 on white is 7:1 for AAA.
- [CSS Minifier: Minify & Compress CSS Online Free](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/css-minifier/): Minifies CSS in the browser: removes comments (keeps /*! licence comments), whitespace and last semicolons, shortens colours (#ffffff to #fff), numbers (0.50em to .5em) and zero lengths (0px to 0), and drops empty rules, without touching strings, url() values, custom properties or spaces inside calc(). Shows original, minified and gzip size; can also beautify (unminify) CSS. Tested against Bootstrap 5.3.3: 281,046 to 232,701 bytes with identical rendering. CSS is never uploaded.
- [Currency Converter Malaysia: Ringgit Exchange Rate Today (BNM)](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/currency-converter-malaysia/): Malaysian ringgit currency converter using Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) middle rates from the Kuala Lumpur interbank foreign exchange market at 12:00 noon, updated daily by an automated workflow (backup: European Central Bank reference rates). Rates are in ringgit per unit; some currencies (for example Japanese yen, Indonesian rupiah, Korean won, Thai baht, Hong Kong dollar) are quoted per 100 units. Covers the US dollar, Singapore dollar, euro, British pound, Japanese yen, Chinese yuan, Thai baht, Indonesian rupiah, Australian dollar, Saudi riyal, UAE dirham and more. The tool also works out the percentage gap between a money changer's or bank's rate and the BNM middle rate, and the estimated extra cost. BNM rates are indicative reference rates; banks, money changers and card networks apply their own buying and selling rates and fees.
- [Debt Consolidation Calculator Malaysia: Is It Worth It?](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/debt-consolidation-calculator-malaysia/): Compares paying credit card and other debts as they are (monthly interest on the balance; card minimum payment 5% of the balance or RM50, whichever is higher; card finance charges 15%, 17% or 18% a year by repayment record) with consolidating them into one personal loan (flat rate converted to EIR, 0.5% stamp duty). Example: RM15,000 of card debt at 18% paid at the minimum costs RM5,967.05 in interest; a 6% flat, 5-year loan costs RM325 a month with RM4,500 interest and RM75 stamp duty (10.85% EIR), saving RM1,392.05. A RM10,000 card balance at 18% paid at the minimum takes 89 months and RM4,054.96 in interest.
- [Driving Licence Cost Malaysia 2026: JPJ Fees and Renewal](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/driving-licence-cost-malaysia/): Malaysian JPJ driving licence fees, verified 15 October 2026. Learner's Driving Licence (LDL), renewable every 3 or 6 months up to 2 years: B2 RM2; B RM20 (3 months) or RM40 (6 months); D and DA RM30 (3 months) or RM60 (6 months). Probationary Driving Licence (PDL), valid 2 years: B2 RM2, B RM40, D and DA RM60. Competent Driving Licence (CDL), 1 to 10 years: B2 and B RM20 a year, D and DA RM30 a year (example: D for 5 years RM150). Physical licence print RM20 for citizens from 23 January 2026, free for seniors 60+, OKU registered with JKM and Class A/A1; the MyJPJ digital licence is free. International Driving Permit RM150 a year. Minimum age: 16 for motorcycles (B2), 17 for cars (D). Car (D) example: LDL RM30 + PDL RM60 = RM90 in JPJ fees, excluding the driving school package set by each school. B2-to-B upgrade capped at RM160 including the test (from 1 October 2024). A PDL is cancelled if KEJARA demerit points exceed the limit during the 2-year probation. The MyLesen B2 programme gives eligible participants a free B2 licence. Test fees and the 10-year renewal discount could not be confirmed for 2026.
- [Due Date Calculator Malaysia and 98-Day Maternity Leave 2026](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/due-date-calculator-malaysia/): Pregnancy due date and maternity leave calculator for Malaysia, verified 15 October 2026. Due date by Naegele's rule: first day of the last period + 280 days (40 weeks), plus (cycle length − 28) days; example: a last period on 1 January 2026 gives a due date of 8 October 2026, or 10 October for a 30-day cycle and 5 October for a 25-day cycle. Trimesters follow the ACOG convention: second from 14 weeks, third from 28 weeks; early term 37 weeks, full term 39, late term 41, post-term 42. Private-sector maternity leave (Employment Act 1955 as amended, from 1 January 2023; Sabah and Sarawak Labour Ordinances from 1 May 2025): 98 consecutive days, starting no earlier than 30 days before confinement; maternity allowance at the ordinary daily rate of pay (at least RM6 a day) if she worked at least 90 days in the 9 months before confinement and has fewer than 5 surviving children; confinement means a birth after at least 22 weeks of pregnancy; pregnant employees are protected from termination (s.41A). Example: due 8 October 2026, leave from that date ends 13 January 2027; starting 30 days early (8 September 2026) it ends 14 December 2026. Private-sector paternity leave is 7 consecutive days after 12 months of service, up to 5 confinements. Civil servants: 60 to 90 days per birth, up to 360 days in service (PP No. 5/2017); Budget 2027 (9 October 2026) announced 98 days and 490 days, start date not yet announced; civil-service paternity leave 7 days up to 5 times (PP No. 9/2002). The Ministry of Health recommends at least 8 antenatal visits.
- [Education Cost Calculator Malaysia: How Much to Save for University](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/education-cost-calculator-malaysia/): Plans university savings for a child in Malaysia: each year of study costs today's yearly cost (fees and living costs) × (1 + education inflation)^years until that year, and the monthly saving needed from now = the amount needed when university starts (later years discounted at the savings return), less existing savings grown at that return, spread over the months left with monthly compounding. Example: a 5-year-old starting a 4-year degree at 18, costing RM25,000 a year today, with 5% inflation and a 4.10% return (the Simpan SSPN dividend for 2025) and RM5,000 already saved: the degree costs RM203,185 at future prices (RM47,141 in the first year) and needs RM889.77 a month. With nothing saved, starting at birth needs about RM768 a month, at 5 about RM931 and at 12 about RM1,665. Inflation and return are assumptions the user sets.
- [EIS Calculator Malaysia 2026: PERKESO Job Loss Allowance](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/eis-calculator-malaysia/): Calculates PERKESO's Employment Insurance System (EIS, now LINDUNG KERJAYA) benefits after job loss in Malaysia. Job Search Allowance: 80% of the assumed monthly wage in month 1, 50% in month 2, 40% in months 3 and 4 and 30% in months 5 and 6, for 3 to 6 months depending on contributions; wages counted up to the RM6,000 insured ceiling; the first claim needs at least 12 monthly contributions in the 24 months before the job loss and must be made within 60 days. Example: RM3,000 assumed wage for 6 months = RM2,400 + RM1,500 + RM1,200 + RM1,200 + RM900 + RM900 = RM8,100. Under the Employment Insurance System (Amendment) Act 2026, for job loss from 1 October 2026: the Early Re-employment Allowance is 50% of the unpaid allowance (25% before), so someone on RM3,000 re-employed after month 2 gets RM2,100 on top of RM3,900 already paid; training fees up to RM7,000 (was RM4,000) with a RM30 daily allowance; a new RM1,000 Mobility Assistance Allowance for a new job more than 100 km from home. Covered: retrenchment, VSS or MSS, closure, constructive dismissal; not covered: resignation, dismissal for misconduct, retirement. Contributions are 0.2% from the employee and 0.2% from the employer.
- [Employer Cost Calculator Malaysia 2026: EPF, SOCSO, EIS and HRD](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/employer-cost-calculator-malaysia/): Calculates what an employee really costs an employer in Malaysia: wages and fixed allowances, employer EPF (13% for wages up to RM5,000, 12% above; 4% from age 60; 2% for foreign workers from October 2025), employer SOCSO 1.75% (1.25% from age 60) and EIS 0.2% (not for foreign workers) by the contribution schedules, the HRD Corp levy of 1% for employers with 10 or more Malaysian employees in covered sectors or 0.5% voluntary for 5 to 9 (on Malaysian employees' wages only), and EPF on bonus. Example: RM3,000 salary with the 1% HRD levy: EPF RM390, SOCSO RM51.65, EIS RM5.90, HRD RM30, total RM3,477.55 a month (15.9% on top of pay) and RM41,730.60 a year.
- [EPF Calculator Malaysia 2026: KWSP Dividend & Retirement](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/epf-calculator/): Projects EPF (KWSP) savings to age 55 or 60 from age, salary, yearly raise, current balances in Akaun Persaraan, Sejahtera and Fleksibel, own contribution rate and voluntary top-ups, using the KWSP Third Schedule, the 75/15/10 account split and EPF's dividend method; compares the inflation-adjusted result with EPF's Basic (RM390,000), Adequate (RM650,000) and Enhanced (RM1.3 million) benchmarks. Includes dividend history 2016–2025 (2025: 6.15%).
- [EV vs Petrol Cost Calculator Malaysia 2026: Home, Public, BUDI95](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/ev-vs-petrol-cost-calculator-malaysia/): EV versus petrol running cost calculator for Malaysia, verified 15 October 2026. Home charging is priced as the rise in the TNB bill under the RP4 domestic tariff (energy 27.03 sen, capacity 4.55 sen, network 12.85 sen per kWh, minus the Energy Efficiency Incentive, which shrinks as use rises, KWTBB 1.6% above 300 kWh, SST above the protection level); there is no EV-specific domestic tariff. Example: a 400 kWh a month home adding 170 kWh for an EV sees its bill rise by about RM94, roughly 55 sen per kWh, above the base rate because the efficiency incentive falls. Public charging prices are not regulated (MITI, July 2026) and are set by operators: published examples AC about RM1.00 to RM1.15 per kWh, DC RM1.30 to RM1.80 per kWh; Tesla Superchargers for non-Tesla EVs RM1.80. Petrol follows the Ministry of Finance's weekly prices: BUDI95 RON95 at RM1.99 a litre up to 300 litres a month, the unsubsidised price above the quota. Example at 1,500 km a month, an EV at 14.2 kWh/100 km (80% home charging, public at RM1.40) against a Proton Saga at 4.9 L/100 km: with BUDI95 petrol costs about the same as the EV; unsubsidised (RON95 RM4.62 on 15 October 2026) the EV saves about RM186 a month. EV consumption figures are battery capacity ÷ WLTP range; real-world use is usually higher.
- [EXIF Editor Online: View and Edit Photo Metadata, Add Copyright](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/exif-editor/): Free browser-based EXIF editor and viewer for JPEG, PNG and WebP. Shows every EXIF, GPS, XMP, IPTC and PNG text field with a privacy summary; edits camera make and model, lens, software, date taken, orientation and GPS (add, change or remove), removes serial numbers, owner name and the embedded thumbnail, and writes the five IPTC photo metadata fields Google Images reads (Creator dc:creator, Credit Line photoshop:Credit, Copyright Notice dc:rights, Web Statement of Rights xmpRights:WebStatement, Licensor URL plus:LicensorURL) as XMP, plus title, description and keywords. Edits rewrite only the metadata blocks, so image data is copied byte for byte with no quality loss. Can stamp the same copyright on many photos and download a ZIP. Google says EXIF is not a ranking factor; the IPTC rights fields control the credit and Licensable badge in Google Images. Files are never uploaded.
- [EXIF Remover: Remove Metadata and GPS From Photos Online](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/exif-remover/): Free browser-based EXIF and metadata remover for JPEG, PNG and WebP, single files or batches downloaded as a ZIP. Lists what each photo reveals (GPS location, date taken, camera, serial numbers, owner name, software, embedded thumbnail, XMP edit history, IPTC, PNG text such as Stable Diffusion prompts, C2PA Content Credentials, data after the image end such as motion-photo video) and removes it losslessly: the compressed image data is copied byte for byte, so quality is unchanged. - [Faraid Calculator Malaysia: Islamic Inheritance Shares (Shafi'i)](https://tool.thebukitbesi.com/faraid-calculator/): Faraid (Islamic inheritance) calculator under the Shafi'i school as practised in Malaysia, verified 15 October 2026. Fixed shares (ashab al-furud): husband 1/2 with no child or son's child, 1/4 with one; wife or wives (shared) 1/4 or 1/8; father 1/6 with a son, 1/6 + residue with only daughters, the residue with no child; mother 1/6 with a child or two or more siblings, 1/3 otherwise, and 1/3 of the remainder in the Umariyyatain (spouse + father + mother: husband 1/2, mother 1/6, father 1/3; wife 1/4, mother 1/4, father 1/2); daughter 1/2 alone, 2/3 for two or more, residuary 2:1 with a son; son's daughter 1/6 with one daughter (takmilah); grandmother 1/6; uterine siblings 1/6 or 1/3; full sister 1/2 or 2/3, or residuary with daughters. Residuaries in order: son, son's son, father, grandfather, full brother, consanguine brother, nephews, uncles, cousins. 'Awl when the shares exceed the estate (wife + father + mother + 2 daughters: base 24 raised to 27, wife 1/9; husband + 2 sisters raised to 7). Musytarakah: full siblings share the 1/3 with uterine siblings. In Malaysia a residue with no residuary goes to Baitulmal (a wife alone gets 1/4, Baitulmal 3/4); Perlis (2018 fatwa) returns it to the fixed heirs other than the spouse (radd). Before faraid: funeral costs, debts, harta sepencarian and a bequest to non-heirs of up to 1/3. Example: an RM300,000 estate less RM5,000 funeral and RM10,000 debts = RM285,000 for a wife, mother, one son and two daughters: wife 1/8 RM35,625, mother 1/6 RM47,500, son RM100,937.50, each daughter RM50,468.75. Grandfather with siblings (muqasamah) cases need a Syariah Court ruling. Small estates up to RM5 million go to the JKPTG estate distribution unit; movable estates up to RM600,000 to Amanah Raya.

Under the relied-upon Shafi'i view, delaying the qada past the next Ramadan without a valid reason adds one fidyah a day for every Ramadan passed; those unable to fast (old age, chronic illness) pay one fidyah a day without qada; pregnant or nursing women who did not fast for fear for the child make up the fast and pay one fidyah a day.
